items.title: Regression when using attributes as part of scope
items.body:
When using `{attributes: {include: [...]}` as part of a scope, the query crashes with ```Unhandled rejection TypeError: include.attributes.map is not a function``` resulting from the expectation that attributes is an array on #1129 of query-generator.js. 

This used to work just fine.

## What you are doing?
Setting the following as a scope. 
```js
          return {
            attributes: {
              include: [
                [sequelize.literal('(select "organisation_participation_id" from "participations" where "session_id" = "'+session_referencer+'.Session"."id" and "role" = \'owner\')'), 'owner']
              ]
            }
          };
```

## What do you expect to happen?
I expect the attributes specified to be included. 

## What is actually happening?

items.title: [regression] Operator symbols not enumerable in `for .. in` loops!
items.body:
*EDIT: I initially thought the new *Operator Symbols* introduced in 4.12.0 were only incompatible with `_.isEmpty`. I quickly realized they're incompatible with `for .. in` loops and the implications are far more serious!*

I've found an important regression that occurred when Operator Symbols were introduced in 4.12.0: every time `_.isEmpty` is used against an object that contains only Symbol keyed props, it returns `true` :-(
Indeed, [isEmpty's documentation](https://lodash.com/docs/4.17.4#isEmpty) states that *"Objects are considered empty if they have no own enumerable **string** keyed properties."* (emphasis is mine).

The first important regression I've spotted is when using the paranoid option on a model. The function [`_paranoidClause`](https://github.com/sequelize/sequelize/blob/master/lib/model.js#L52) might override `options.where` because of the incorrect result of [`_.isEmpty(options.where)`](https://github.com/sequelize/sequelize/blob/master/lib/model.js#L86). In my app, where I constantly use this option, many queries were completely messed up.

Other occurrences of _.isEmtpy might introduce equally severe regressions. I advise we replace them all with a custom implementation of that method.

I'll try to find some time to write a first PR fixing this in the evening, if no one else does.
